title: 14-Day Italy Itinerary: Rome, Florence, Venice & the Amalfi Coast: The Ultimate Two-Week Italy Trip
description: Two weeks covering Italy's greatest hits — ancient Rome, Renaissance Florence, romantic Venice, and the stunning Amalfi Coast. This classic route connects Italy's most iconic destinations by high-speed train and ferry, with enough time to savor each stop without rushing.

days.title: Arrive in Rome — Heart of the Eternal City

activities.name: Walk the Centro Storico
activities.description: Settle into your hotel near Piazza Navona or Trastevere. Once refreshed, take the classic Rome walk: start at the Spanish Steps, toss a coin at the Trevi Fountain, then stand in awe inside the Pantheon — 2,000 years old and still the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome.
details: 📍 Spanish Steps → Trevi Fountain → Pantheon → Piazza Navona (~2.5km walk)
💡 Visit Trevi Fountain after 8pm for smaller crowds and magical lighting
⏱️ Allow 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace

days.title: Ancient Rome — Colosseum, Forum & Palatine Hill

activities.name: The Colosseum & Roman Forum
activities.description: Book the Full Experience ticket (€24) for underground + arena floor access — worth every cent. Start early (8:30am opening) to beat tour groups. After the Colosseum, walk through the Roman Forum and up Palatine Hill for sweeping views over ancient Rome.
details: 🎫 Book at colosseo.it — sells out weeks ahead
⏱️ Allow 3–4 hours for Colosseum + Forum + Palatine
💡 The underground gladiator tunnels are the highlight

activities.name: Capitoline Museums & Altare della Patria
activities.description: Walk along Via dei Fori Imperiali to the Capitoline Museums — Rome's oldest public museum with Caravaggio, the Dying Gaul, and the she-wolf statue. Take the free elevator to the top of the Altare della Patria for a 360° panorama.
details: 💡 The Capitoline rooftop cafe has views over the Forum
📍 Piazza del Campidoglio (designed by Michelangelo)

activities.name: Sunset in Trastevere
activities.description: Cross the Tiber to Trastevere — Rome's most charming neighborhood. Wander cobblestone alleys, pop into Santa Maria in Trastevere (stunning gold mosaics), and end with gelato from Fatamorgana.

activities.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
activities.description: Enter at 8am (first slot). Rush through the galleries to reach the Sistine Chapel before crowds — Michelangelo's ceiling is overwhelming in person. Then exit through St. Peter's Basilica (free entry, separate line). Climb the dome (551 steps) for the best view in Rome.
details: 🎫 Book at museivaticani.va — €17 online
⏱️ Allow 3–4 hours total
💡 Take the shortcut door from Sistine Chapel directly into St. Peter's (guided tours only)
👗 Shoulders and knees covered — mandatory

activities.name: Borghese Gallery
activities.description: Timed entry only, 2-hour slots. Houses Bernini's Apollo and Daphne, David, and Caravaggio masterpieces. Small but absolutely world-class — every piece is a showstopper.
details: 🎫 Book at galleriaborghese.beniculturali.it — sells out fast
💡 The 5pm slot has the best light through the windows

activities.name: Aperitivo Hour
activities.description: Romans do aperitivo from 6–8pm. Head to the Prati neighborhood near the Vatican for craft cocktails at Il Sorpasso — great spritz selection with generous snack platters.

days.title: Train to Naples — Pompeii & Transfer to Sorrento

activities.name: High-Speed Train to Naples
activities.description: Take the Frecciarossa from Roma Termini to Napoli Centrale (1h10m, ~€20–45). Store luggage at the station, then catch the Circumvesuviana train to Pompeii Scavi (35 min, €3.60).
details: 🚄 Book on trenitalia.com or italotreno.it
💡 Buy Circumvesuviana tickets at the Garibaldi underground station (below Centrale)

activities.name: Pompeii Archaeological Park
activities.description: Walk streets frozen in time since 79 AD. Don't miss the Forum, House of the Faun, Garden of the Fugitives (plaster casts of victims), and the remarkably preserved Thermopolium (ancient fast-food counter). Hire an audio guide — context makes it 10x better.
details: 🎫 €18 — book at ticketone.it
⏱️ Allow 3–4 hours minimum
💡 Enter through Porta Marina (main entrance) for a logical route
🧴 Bring water and sunscreen — zero shade

activities.name: Transfer to Sorrento
activities.description: Circumvesuviana from Pompeii to Sorrento (30 min). Check into your hotel overlooking the Bay of Naples. Sorrento is your base for the Amalfi Coast — perched on cliffs with orange and lemon groves everywhere.
details: 💡 Stay in or near Piazza Tasso for easy access to buses and ferries

activities.name: Ferry to Capri
activities.description: Take the first high-speed ferry from Sorrento to Capri (20 min, ~€22). Head straight to the Blue Grotto — small rowboats take you into a cave where the water glows electric blue. Go early before the line wraps around the island.
details: 🚢 Ferries depart from Marina Piccola, Sorrento — buy at dock or caremar.it
💡 Blue Grotto: €18 entry + €15 boat. Often closed in rough seas — check weather
⏱️ Allow 1.5 hours for the full Blue Grotto experience

activities.name: Capri Town & Gardens of Augustus
activities.description: Take the funicular up to Capri Town. Stroll the Piazzetta (the island's glamorous living room), then walk to the Gardens of Augustus for jaw-dropping views of the Faraglioni sea stacks and Via Krupp's hairpin switchbacks.
details: 💡 Walk the Via Krupp path down to Marina Piccola if it's open (free)
📍 Gardens of Augustus: €1 entry

activities.name: Anacapri & Monte Solaro
activities.description: Bus to Anacapri (the quieter, higher village). Take the chairlift to Monte Solaro (€12 round trip) — the island's highest point with 360° views stretching to Vesuvius, the Amalfi Coast, and on clear days, the coast of Calabria.
details: 💡 Walk down from the summit through the forest path (~45 min) to skip the chairlift return

activities.name: Return to Sorrento
activities.description: Catch a late afternoon ferry back. Evening free to explore Sorrento's lively Corso Italia or enjoy limoncello on your hotel terrace.

days.title: Amalfi Coast Drive — Positano, Amalfi & Ravello

activities.name: SITA Bus to Positano
activities.description: Catch the early SITA bus from Sorrento to Positano (1 hour, €2.40). Sit on the right side for the cliffside views. Positano tumbles down the cliffside in a cascade of pastel buildings — it's as stunning as the photos suggest. Walk down through boutique-lined stairs to Spiaggia Grande (main beach). The Path of the Gods hike starts nearby — a 7.8km clifftop trail with Amalfi Coast panoramas. Otherwise, wander the vertical village, shop for handmade sandals, and soak in the views.
details: 💡 Buy bus tickets at tabacchi shops (tobacco/newspaper stands), not on the bus
💡 Alternative: hire a private boat for ~€200 to cruise the coast — worth it for a splurge
👟 Path of the Gods: 3–4 hours, moderate difficulty. Starts in Bomerano (bus from Amalfi)
📍 Fornillo Beach is less crowded than Spiaggia Grande

activities.name: Ferry to Amalfi & Bus to Ravello
activities.description: Take the ferry from Positano to Amalfi (25 min, €9). Explore the striking 9th-century Duomo di Amalfi and its Cloister of Paradise. Then bus up the winding road to Ravello (25 min) — a hilltop town famous for gardens and music.
details: 📍 Amalfi's Paper Museum (Museo della Carta) is a quirky hidden gem
💡 In Ravello, visit Villa Rufolo gardens (€10) — Wagner was inspired here

activities.name: Sunset Cocktails at Palazzo Avino, Ravello
activities.description: The terrace bar at Palazzo Avino has one of Italy's most spectacular sunset views — the entire Amalfi Coast spread below you as the sky turns gold. Book a table and nurse a Negroni.
details: 💡 Call ahead to Antonio at Palazzo Avino for a terrace table

activities.name: Train to Florence
activities.description: Circumvesuviana from Sorrento to Naples (1h), then high-speed Frecciarossa to Firenze SMN (2h45m). Total travel ~4.5 hours — an early start gets you to Florence by lunch.
details: 🚄 Total cost: ~€45–70 (Circumvesuviana + high-speed)
💡 Book the high-speed leg in advance for best prices

activities.name: Florence First Walk — Duomo & Piazza della Signoria
activities.description: Drop bags at your hotel (stay near Santa Croce or Oltrarno for authenticity). Walk to the Duomo — Brunelleschi's dome is the city's crown jewel. Then continue to Piazza della Signoria (outdoor sculpture gallery), cross the Ponte Vecchio (goldsmith shops since 1345), and wander into the Oltrarno neighborhood.
details: 🎫 Duomo dome climb: €30, book at duomo.firenze.it — 463 steps, no elevator
💡 The Baptistery's Gates of Paradise doors are stunning (copies outside, originals in Duomo Museum)
📍 Ponte Vecchio is most magical at golden hour

activities.name: Sunset from Piazzale Michelangelo
activities.description: Walk (or bus #12) up to Piazzale Michelangelo for the iconic Florence panorama — the Duomo, Palazzo Vecchio tower, and Ponte Vecchio all in one frame, backed by the Tuscan hills. Bring a bottle of wine.
details: 💡 Continue up to San Miniato al Monte church for even better views with fewer crowds

activities.name: Uffizi Gallery
activities.description: Book the first slot (8:15am). The Uffizi houses the world's greatest collection of Renaissance art — Botticelli's Birth of Venus and Primavera, Leonardo's Annunciation, Raphael, Titian, and Caravaggio. Don't try to see everything — pick your highlights.
details: 🎫 €25 — book at uffizi.it months ahead
⏱️ Allow 2.5–3 hours
💡 Room 10-14 (Botticelli) and Room 35 (Caravaggio) are the stars

activities.name: Accademia Gallery — Michelangelo's David
activities.description: The David in person is staggering — 5.17 meters of marble perfection. Book your timed entry and allow 1–1.5 hours. The unfinished Prisoners (slaves emerging from stone) leading to David are almost as moving. Cross back to the Oltrarno (south bank) — Florence's artisan quarter. Pop into leather workshops, bookbinders, and frame makers along Via Maggio and Borgo San Frediano. This is the real Florence, away from tour groups.
details: 🎫 €16 — book at galleriaaccademiafirenze.it
💡 The hall with the Prisoners → David reveal is intentionally dramatic
💡 Scuola del Cuoio (leather school) inside Santa Croce church offers tours

days.title: Tuscan Day Trip — Chianti Wine Country

activities.name: Drive into Chianti
activities.description: Rent a car for the day (or join a group tour, ~€60–80pp). The SR222 Chiantigiana road from Florence to Siena winds through cypress-lined hills, vineyards, and medieval hilltop towns. First stop: Greve in Chianti — the region's unofficial capital.
details: 🚗 Car rental from Florence center: ~€50–70/day (Europcar, Hertz near SMN station)
💡 If not driving, Chianti group tours depart from Florence's Santa Maria Novella area

activities.name: Wine Tasting at a Chianti Estate
activities.description: Book a tasting at Castello di Verrazzano or Antinori nel Chianti Classico. Learn about Sangiovese grapes, tour the cellars, and taste 3–5 wines with local cheeses and olive oil. The Antinori winery is a stunning modern building built into the hillside.
details: 🍷 Tastings: €25–50pp depending on estate and package
💡 Antinori has a restaurant with panoramic views — book for lunch if possible

activities.name: Hilltop Villages
activities.description: Drive to Castellina in Chianti — a compact medieval town with an underground tunnel street (Via delle Volte) and panoramic fortress. If time allows, detour to Radda in Chianti for more village charm and a gelato in the piazza.
details: 💡 Buy Chianti Classico wines directly from producers — much cheaper than in Florence

activities.name: Return to Florence
activities.description: Drive back via the scenic route. Evening free in Florence — try a late-night gelato at Vivoli (Italy's oldest gelateria) or craft cocktails at Mad Souls & Spirits in Oltrarno.

days.title: Florence to Venice — Arrival on the Water

activities.name: High-Speed Train to Venice
activities.description: Frecciarossa from Firenze SMN to Venezia Santa Lucia (2h, ~€25–50). When you step out of the station, the Grand Canal is right there — your first view of Venice hits differently.
details: 💡 Stay in Dorsoduro or Cannaregio for a more local experience (avoid San Marco hotels — overpriced)
🚢 Get a 72-hour vaporetto pass (€40) — unlimited water bus travel

activities.name: Grand Canal & Rialto Bridge
activities.description: Take Vaporetto Line 1 down the Grand Canal — it's a €7.50 water bus ride that feels like a private tour past Renaissance palazzos. Hop off at Rialto to explore the iconic bridge and the morning fish market (Mercato di Rialto, open till early afternoon). Put away Google Maps and deliberately get lost. Venice rewards wandering — you'll stumble onto hidden squares (campi), quiet canals, and tiny bridges that no guidebook covers. Head toward Campo Santa Margherita in Dorsoduro — a lively student square with great aperitivo bars.
details: 💡 Vaporetto Line 1 is the slow local — Line 2 is express. Take Line 1 for the full experience
📍 The Rialto fish market is best before noon
💡 Campo Santa Margherita is Venice's most authentic, non-touristy square

activities.name: Sunset at Zattere
activities.description: Walk the Fondamenta delle Zattere — a long south-facing waterfront promenade in Dorsoduro. Watch the sunset over Giudecca island with a gelato from Nico (their gianduiotto — frozen chocolate hazelnut on whipped cream — is legendary).

days.title: Venice — St. Mark's, Doge's Palace & Islands

activities.name: St. Mark's Basilica & Doge's Palace
activities.description: Arrive at Piazza San Marco by 8:30am (before cruise ship crowds). The basilica's gold mosaics are breathtaking — pay €7 for rooftop terrace access (the view over the piazza is incredible). Then tour the Doge's Palace — the seat of Venetian power for 700 years. Walk across the enclosed Bridge of Sighs.
details: 🎫 St. Mark's: free entry (but book skip-the-line at €3). Rooftop terrace: €7
🎫 Doge's Palace: €30 — book at palazzoducale.visitmuve.it
💡 The Secret Itineraries tour (€35) accesses hidden rooms and Casanova's prison cell

activities.name: Murano & Burano Islands
activities.description: Take the vaporetto to Murano (15 min) — watch master glassblowers create art in 1,000°C furnaces. Then continue to Burano (30 min) — a technicolor fishing village where every house is painted a different shade. Burano is absurdly photogenic.
details: 🚢 Vaporetto Line 12 runs Fondamente Nove → Murano → Burano
💡 In Murano, visit the Glass Museum (€12) or just watch free demos at workshops
💡 In Burano, look for handmade lace (traditional craft) and eat at Da Romano

activities.name: Gondola Ride at Dusk
activities.description: Yes, it's touristy. Yes, it's expensive. Yes, you should do it anyway. A 30-minute gondola ride through quiet backwater canals at dusk is genuinely magical. Standard rate: €80 daytime / €100 after 7pm (for up to 6 people — split with other couples).
details: 💡 Request the smaller canals, not the Grand Canal — much more atmospheric
💡 Gondola stands near Santa Maria Formosa or San Tomà are less touristy than San Marco

activities.name: Cannaregio & the Jewish Ghetto
activities.description: Explore Cannaregio — Venice's most residential sestiere. Visit the Jewish Ghetto (the world's first — the word 'ghetto' originated here in 1516). Tour the synagogues and the small but powerful museum. Then walk along Fondamenta della Misericordia — lined with bacari and local restaurants.
details: 🎫 Jewish Museum + synagogue tour: €12
💡 Fondamenta della Misericordia is where young Venetians eat and drink — zero tourists

activities.name: Peggy Guggenheim Collection or Scuola Grande di San Rocco
activities.description: Choose your vibe: Peggy Guggenheim Collection (modern art — Pollock, Dalí, Kandinsky in a Grand Canal palazzo) or Scuola Grande di San Rocco (Tintoretto's masterpiece cycle — Venice's answer to the Sistine Chapel). Both take 1.5–2 hours.
details: 🎫 Guggenheim: €16 · San Rocco: €10
💡 Guggenheim's garden terrace overlooking the Grand Canal is perfect for a breather

activities.name: Final Venice Evening
activities.description: Take one last wander through Venice at night — the city transforms when day-trippers leave. The quiet canals, lamplight reflecting on water, and distant echoes of footsteps create an atmosphere like nowhere else on earth.

days.title: Day Trip to Verona or Padua

activities.name: Train to Verona
activities.description: Quick train from Venice to Verona (1h15m, ~€10–20). Verona is Shakespeare's city — home of Romeo and Juliet — but it's also a gorgeous Roman-era city with a stunning arena, world-class dining, and far fewer tourists than Venice. The Arena di Verona is a 2,000-year-old Roman amphitheater that still hosts opera performances today. Walk inside (€10) and imagine gladiators, then browse the elegant shops lining Piazza Bra.
details: 💡 Alternative: Padua (30 min from Venice) for Giotto's Scrovegni Chapel — a must for art lovers
🚄 Regional trains are cheap (~€10) — no need for high-speed
🎫 Arena: €10 · Open daily 8:30am–7:30pm
🎶 Summer opera season (June–September) is legendary — book at arena.it

activities.name: Old Town Walk
activities.description: Walk through Piazza delle Erbe (daily market since Roman times), past Juliet's Balcony (Casa di Giulietta — touristy but fun), up the Torre dei Lamberti for panoramic views, and across the Ponte Pietra Roman bridge.
details: 📍 Juliet's Balcony: Via Cappello 23 (free courtyard, €6 for balcony)
💡 Piazza delle Erbe was Verona's Roman forum — note the ancient fountain

activities.name: Castel San Pietro Viewpoint
activities.description: Cross the river and climb to Castel San Pietro for the best panoramic view of Verona — the Arena, red rooftops, and the Adige River curving through the city. Perfect spot for photos.
details: 💡 There's a funicular if you don't want to climb (€2)

activities.name: Return to Venice
activities.description: Train back to Venice. Last night — make it count with a final aperitivo on the Grand Canal.

days.title: Departure Day — Last Morning in Italy

activities.name: Early Morning Venice Walk
activities.description: Wake up early for one final stroll through empty Venice — this is when the city belongs to its residents. Watch fishermen unload at the Rialto market, grab a coffee at a neighborhood bar, and soak in the silence before the world wakes up.
details: 💡 The Rialto fish market is most alive from 7–9am
☕ Stand at the bar for espresso like a local — €1.20 vs €5 sitting down

activities.name: Transfer to Airport
activities.description: Take the Alilaguna water bus (€15, 1h15m — scenic route through the lagoon) or the ACTV bus from Piazzale Roma (€8, 25 min) to Marco Polo Airport. Or splurge on a water taxi (€120 — arrive by boat directly to the terminal).
details: 💡 Allow 2.5 hours before your flight — Venice transfers take longer than you expect
💡 If flying from Venice, Marco Polo (VCE) is the main airport. Treviso (TSF) is budget airlines only
